creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 5. An accumulator whose name shadows a module-level variable or a builtin collects nothing, and overwrites the outer binding on the way past.

```rad
tally = ["module", "level"]

fn f():
    tally = []
    tally += ["from-fn"]
    print("  local inside fn :", tally)   // [ ]

f()
print("module after :", tally)            // [ "from-fn" ]
```

The read resolves to the fresh local; the write lands on the module binding.

Builtins occupy that outer scope too, which is the form that cost an hour. This helper always returns `[]`:

```rad
fn pids_where(commands, predicate):
    matches = []
    for pid, cmd in commands:
        if predicate(cmd):
            matches += [pid]
    return matches
```

The `if` body demonstrably runs - a `print` inside it fires - and `matches.len()` is 0 on the next line. `rad check` reports no diagnostics. Renaming to `found` fixes it with nothing else changed. Same for `keys`, `filter`, `count`, `sort`, `unique`, `join`.

The write then takes the builtin out for the rest of the script: after a function does `keys += [1]`, calling `keys({"a": 1})` fails with RAD30001.

Only `+=` is affected, across every type. `x = x + y` is a correct workaround and `x += y` is not, which is the reverse of what the two shapes suggest.

Adjacent to #151.1 (write semantics of globals inside `fn`) but narrower and more mechanical: one compound assignment resolving its read and its write in different scopes. Worth fixing whichever way the broader globals question lands, since either way the two halves should agree.

A checker rule for a local shadowing a builtin catches the expensive half cheaply - those names are all known at parse time.

---

### Orientation

- The bug is runtime scope resolution in `core/` (the tree-walking interpreter). `rts/` is only involved because it desugars the syntax: `rts/converter.go:178` `convertCompoundAssign` rewrites `x += y` into `Assign(x, x + y)` and sets `assign.UpdateEnclosing = true`. `rts/converter.go:201` `convertIncrDecr` does the same for `x++`, so `x++` carries the identical bug shape.
- The read path is `Env.GetVar` (innermost-first, `core/env.go:45`). The write path is `Env.setVar` with `updateEnclosing=true` (`core/env.go:79`), which ascends the chain *before* consulting the local frame. That asymmetry is the whole bug.
- Builtins live in the root `Env.Vars` alongside module-level variables (`core/interpreter.go:120` `InitBuiltIns` seeds every `FunctionsByName` entry). So a fn-local named after a builtin is just an ordinary outer binding to ascend into, and the write replaces the builtin's `RadFn` value.
- The static checker already models this correctly and disagrees with the runtime. `rts/check/binder.go:475` `declareTarget` resolves an `UpdateEnclosing` target with `b.current.Lookup(name)`, which is innermost-first. Builtins there live in a *separate* builtin scope (`rts/check/binder.go:108` `ensureBuiltin`), never in the file scope, which is why the checker cannot see the clobber at all. Remember rts must not import core.

### Where to start

- `core/env.go:79` `setVar`. It ascends whenever `e.Enclosing.Vars[name]` exists, with no check on `e.Vars[name]` first. Checking the local frame first is the fix.
- `core/env.go:37` `SetVar` and `core/env.go:41` `SetVarUpdatingEnclosing` are the two entry points into it.
- `core/interpreter.go:982` `doVarPathAssign` threads `updateEnclosing` through; it originates from `Assign.UpdateEnclosing` at `core/interpreter.go:837-839`.
- Confirmed against `bin/radd` v0.11.0. A fn-local with no enclosing binding of the same name works fine, so the trigger is strictly "an outer binding of that name exists":

```rad
fn d():
    keys = []
    keys += [1]
    return keys
print(d())             // [ ]
print(keys({"a": 1}))  // error[RAD30001]: Cannot invoke 'keys' as a function: it is a list
```

- Correction to the card's scope: `+=` is not the only affected form. `x++` goes through `convertIncrDecr`, which sets the same flag, and reproduces identically on v0.11.0 - `zzz = 0` at module level, then a fn doing `zzz = 10; zzz++; return zzz` returns `10` and leaves the module binding at `11`. Any fix has to cover incr/decr.
- For the checker rule (local shadowing a builtin): `rts/check/binder.go:187` `addIssue` is the hook, `rts/check/check.go:154` `addBindIssues` surfaces it, and `rts/check/binder.go:233` (`ErrHoistedFunctionShadowsArgument`) is the nearest precedent. A new code must be allocated in the 4xxxx band in `rts/rl/errors.go` - the highest in use is `ErrIntLiteralOutOfRange = "40015"`, and numbers are never reused.

### How to verify

- `make build` produces `bin/radd`. Run repros with `./bin/radd script.rad`.
- Snapshot cases go under `core/testing/snapshots/`; the scope and assignment cases live in `control_flow` and `operators`. Update with `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=control_flow` (the `=` is required; a bare `-update` swallows `-run`).
- The binder already asserts the intended semantics in `rts/check/binder_test.go:150` ("`+=` and friends set UpdateEnclosing: they must NOT introduce a..."). Run `go test ./rts/check/`.
- Full loop: `make all`.

### Done when

- A fn-local shadowing a module-level variable accumulates into the local and leaves the outer binding untouched.
- Same for a fn-local shadowing a builtin, and the builtin stays callable afterwards.
- `x++` and `x--` behave identically to `x += 1`.
- `total += x` inside `if` and `for` bodies still writes the enclosing binding - that is the behavior `UpdateEnclosing` exists for. Snapshot cases in both directions.
- If the checker rule ships: new code in `rts/rl/errors.go`, doc at `core/error_docs/<code>.md`, `make generate` run, `make verify-generated` clean, and a case under `rts/check/snapshots/`.

### Watch out for

- `rts` must not import `core`, so a checker rule needs the builtin name list from `rts/embedded/functions.txt` (generated by `function-metadata/extract.go` via `make generate`), not from `core.FunctionsByName`.
- `docs-web/docs/reference/errors.md` and `core/embedded_docs/` are generated. Edit `core/error_docs/<code>.md` (style guide in `core/error_docs/AGENTS.md`) and run `make generate`.
- `setVar` is on the path of every assignment in the language. Loop-variable writes (`core/interpreter.go:1132`, `:1188`) and loop-context writes use plain `SetVar` with `updateEnclosing=false` and should be unaffected, but they share the function - check them in the snapshot run.
title: Fix += reading the function-local but writing the enclosing binding
